title: Key-Value Store System Card
source: Chandramouli et al., FASTER: A Concurrent Key-Value Store with In-Place Updates, SIGMOD 2018

operations: Read: Read the value corresponding to a key.
Upsert: Replace the value corresponding to a key with a new value blindly (i.e. regardless of the existing value). Insert as new, if the key does not exist.

RMW: Update the value of a key based on the existing value and an input using update logic provided at compile-time. The user also provides an initial value for the update, which is used when a key does not exist in the store.
Delete: Delete a key from the store.
api.key_semantics: Keys are opaque uint64_t values. The store must handle any key distribution -- keys may be sparse, non-sequential, or randomly distributed across the full uint64_t range.

concurrency: The store must support concurrent access from multiple threads and scale with increasing thread count.

consistency_and_recovery.monotonicity_property: For any two update requests r1 and r2 issued (in order) by a thread, the state after recovery includes the effects of (1) none; (2) only r1; or (3) both r1 and r2. In other words, the state after recovery cannot include the effects of r2 without also including r1.
consistency_and_recovery.checkpointing: The store must support a Checkpoint() operation that persists the current state to disk. Applications can periodically obtain a fuzzy checkpoint of the store.
consistency_and_recovery.read_correctness: Concurrent reads must never observe torn or corrupted values while other threads are performing updates.

memory_constraint.note: primary_scenario_gb lists the budgets you will be benchmarked at (optimization targets). mem_budget_bytes is passed at runtime via InitExtended() and may be ANY value. ALL data-structure sizing (hash buckets, cache entries, buffer pool pages, etc.) MUST be computed from mem_budget_bytes at runtime, not hardcoded for a specific budget.
memory_constraint.storage_path: Directory for disk-backed storage, provided via InitExtended()
memory_constraint.ssd_specs: NVMe SSD at /mnt/ssd. Sequential read: ~3 GB/s. Sequential write: ~2 GB/s. Random 4KB read: ~500K IOPS. Random 4KB write: ~200K IOPS.

hardware.cpu: 64 vCPU (2 sockets x 16 cores x 2 HT)
hardware.memory: 256 GB DDR4 (store budget may be limited via mem_budget_bytes)
hardware.numa: 2 NUMA nodes; benchmark runs on NUMA node 0

allowed_libraries: POSIX file I/O (open, pread, pwrite, fdatasync)

optimization_objective: Maximize total operations per second across all threads.

design_space.note: Fully open -- any architecture is acceptable provided it satisfies the full API (including Delete), concurrency, the monotonicity property, read correctness, and memory constraint above. Novel designs are encouraged.
